proof_nl: Let x be any real number, and set m = floor(x). By the definition of the floor function, m is an integer, m ≤ x, and m is the greatest integer with this property. We claim that x < m + 1. If not, then x ≥ m + 1. Since m + 1 is also an integer and m + 1 ≤ x, this would contradict the maximality of m as the greatest integer less than or equal to x. Therefore x < m + 1 = floor(x) + 1. Since x was arbitrary, the statement holds for all real x.
solver_summary: For m = floor(x), maximality of the floor implies m+1 cannot still be ≤ x; hence x < m+1 = floor(x)+1.
vetter_reason: The proof correctly applies the definition of floor(x): letting m = floor(x), one has m ≤ x and m is the greatest integer ≤ x. Assuming x ≥ m + 1 implies that m + 1 is an integer with m + 1 ≤ x, contradicting maximality. Therefore x < floor(x) + 1 for all real x.
